Command: Do Not Serve God and Money
Summary: Jesus' loyalty command: no one can serve two masters; lay up treasure in heaven rather than on earth, where moth and rust corrupt.
Commandment: Lay not up treasures on earth, but lay up treasures in heaven; no man can serve God and mammon.
Application: Where treasure goes, the heart follows. The command exposes divided loyalty: wealth is a rival master, not a neutral tool, when it commands obedience.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: 'where your treasure is, there will your heart be also' (Matthew 6:21).
Function: No one can serve two masters, and Jesus names the rival plainly. A New Testament command, not a Mosaic one — the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it. Its goal was undivided loyalty: treasure laid up in heaven rather than on earth, where moth and rust corrupt. The evil it addressed was wealth as a rival master — a treasure that commands obedience and drags the heart after it. It restrained that evil by the test Jesus gives: where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
